x: Remedy Entertainment's benchmark, made with VNU European Labs and given away on magazine cover discs. The team behind it would go on to found Futuremark.
The founding team sets up in Espoo, Finland. UL's own timeline says the official company papers arrived on New Year's Eve 1997.
Futuremark formally launches.
Futuremark's own press release: "the world's first 3D benchmark aimed directly at the 3D gaming community". DirectX 6, on Remedy's MAX-FX engine.
DirectX 7 and hardware transform and lighting. UL's timeline says it arrived "just in time for Christmas".
First benchmark with vertex and pixel shaders; the last to use Remedy's MAX-FX engine.
The company that traded as MadOnion.com settles on the name Futuremark Corporation.
First DirectX 9 3DMark and the first to include CPU tests.

Futuremark publishes an audit listing eight places where Nvidia's Detonator FX drivers behaved differently when the benchmark was recognised. ATI admits a smaller tweak. Weeks later Futuremark softens its verdict to 'application specific optimization' while saying rules were broken.
DirectX 9 with Shader Model 2 required for every graphics test.
The engine's first public version; UNIGINE gives 2005 as its founding year. Its roots are Alexander Zapryagaev's open-source frustum.org project, begun in 2002.
The first 3DMark where the CPU result affects the final score.
JeGX of Geeks3D and oZone3D releases a fur-rendering OpenGL benchmark. The developer's own later statement: first released in 2007.
UNIGINE's first benchmark. The company dates it only to 2007.
DirectX 10. Its physics test later becomes a dispute over GPU PhysX.
AMD adds a driver protection keyed on the file name, per Geeks3D, to protect Radeon HD 4850/4870 VRMs.
FurMark's command-line reference already lists /xtreme_burning, 'a mode that overburns the GPU'.
UNIGINE's second benchmark (2008).
The package includes etqw.exe, a copy named after Enemy Territory: Quake Wars, to bypass Catalyst's FurMark detection and get SLI/CrossFire profiles.
Futuremark's free browser benchmark launches. Support ends in July 2015.
Geeks3D reports a monitoring chip that throttles one PowerPlay level when the voltage regulators are overloaded.
UNIGINE announces it as the world's first true DirectX 11 benchmark: tessellated cobblestones, a steampunk village and a dragon.
Futuremark's mobile and embedded unit becomes Rightware.
Heat post-effect, vertex-displacement fur, XML localization. Scores drop because the load is heavier.
Power sensors plus driver detection of FurMark and OCCT. TechPowerUp measures 153 W limited versus 304 W unlimited.
DirectX 11 with tessellation and compute shaders.
Comments on a TechPowerUp poll: fine if you can disable them, not fine as an application blacklist.
Heavier load (a GTX 480 falls from 6478 to 1769 points), dynamic background, two online-score presets.
UNIGINE's first paid edition of a benchmark.
Futuremark sells its game development division to the Angry Birds company.
First version to run on the Mac.
One app, separate tests, Windows, Android and iOS scores comparable for the first time.
Presets, GPU monitoring, improved SSDO and the new Advanced edition.
A forest-covered mountain valley. Lead artist Andrey Kushner: "Living in Siberia, we wanted to show how beautiful the nature is here."
More than 100,000 downloads in its first week, per UL.
Billed as the world's first 4K Ultra HD benchmark.
Underwriters Laboratories buys the company.
"The world's first DirectX 12 API performance test".
The old branch keeps shipping.
Deferred rendering, PBR, geometry water, volumetric clouds, SSRTGI and voxel lighting.
Pascal GP104, 1,920 CUDA cores, 8 GB GDDR5, US$379 partner / $449 Founders Edition. Ten years later, 38 of them are in your test batch.
A pure DirectX 12 engine, free for every Windows edition of 3DMark.
Futuremark answers claims that Time Spy favoured Nvidia: one code path for all vendors, and the driver decides whether queues run in parallel.
GTX 1080/1070/1060, RX 480/470/460 and a 5K resolution.
A lone professor, an abandoned classroom, SSRTGI lighting and an 8K Optimized preset.
"The world's first 4K DirectX 12 benchmark test".
The Futuremark name is retired; R&D stays in Espoo.
UL finds public-app scores up to 47% higher than a private build: the phones recognised the app by name.
The first dedicated real-time ray tracing benchmark for gamers, at 2560 x 1440.
Free VR in Basic, VR on Linux, 16384 x 16384 maximum resolution. Still the latest version.

t: Wild Life and the DXR test
x: Cross-platform Wild Life arrives for Apple, Android and Windows.
Experimental renderers arrive in the engine. Superposition itself has no release that uses them.
DirectX 12 Ultimate, DXR 1.1 and mesh shaders, sponsored by Lenovo Legion. 3DMark's price becomes $34.99.
First beta on the Geeks3D Discord, rebuilt on GeeXLab.
Version 2.0.4.0 adds Linux support.
Ray tracing for phones and thin laptops on Vulkan 1.1, with a 20-minute stress test.
A first beta of a separate ROG version of FurMark 2.
OpenGL 3.2 and Vulkan 1.1, a GUI plus a command-line tool, a new knot scene and online scores.
2.3.0.0: a Pi 5 manages 4 FPS at 1024 x 640, a Pi 4 about 1.
Non-ray-traced, cross-platform, native 4K and about three times heavier than Time Spy. Score = average FPS x 100.
Support for Intel Arc B580 and B570.
JeGX writes that branch 1.39.x is probably the last, with patches only until a final stop.
A native Mac app with Steel Nomad, Solar Bay and Wild Life Extreme.
More ray tracing: reflections on every surface and soft shadows.
Available directly from UL Solutions.
Native 4K plus AI upscaling and frame generation from several vendors. No name or date yet.
Its logo will appear inside the upcoming benchmark.
The 'last' branch is still getting new-GPU support.
Newest Blackwell GPUs; elapsed time shown as days, hours, minutes and seconds.
37 FurMark, 35 Superposition and 35 Steel Nomad scores from three test PCs, cross-checked against public FurMark result pages: 36 match a GTX 1070, one link points at a different GPU.
